summary: The study investigates the effect of impurities on the fixed charge of nanoscale HfO2 films grown by atomic layer deposition (ALD) using two different precursor chemistries—HfCl4 and tetrakis(diethylamido)hafnium (TDEAH). The research highlights the impact of precursor choice on impurity incorporation, which significantly affects the fixed charge and electrical characteristics of the HfO2/SiO2/Si gate stacks.
evidence: HfO2 films were grown by atomic layer deposition using two different precursor chemistries—HfCl4 and tetrakis(diethylamido)hafnium (TDEAH) with H2O as the oxidant. The study shows that the choice of precursors plays an important role in determining the nature and type of impurities incorporated in the dielectric film. The metal precursors used for ALD HfO2 fall into two broad categories—metal halides and metal organics.
